# caffeinity-routing

A goal like "ship my site" or "get hired" crosses several skills, and each one only knows its own
edges. This skill holds the map: twelve numbered brews (Brew 1 to Brew 12; older docs call them W1 to W12), each an ordered list of
skills with what every step receives and what it hands on. Other skills cite these numbers
(`release-gate-chair` implements Brew 3 · Espresso; `seo-crawl` is the first step of Brew 4 · Cold brew), so keep them stable.

Routing is a decision, not the work. Name the workflow, the first step and its input, then hand
off. Doing a step's job here produces a worse version of a skill that already exists.

## Ground rules

- **One skill owns a single-step request.** If the request fits one skill's description, route
  straight to it and stop. A workflow is for goals that need two or more.
- **Name the brew by number and name, and the steps by skill name.** "Brew 4 · Cold brew, step 1: seo-crawl on
  https://example.com" is checkable; "do some SEO first" is not.
- **Never fill a missing step yourself.** Run `scripts/route_check.py` and report what is not
  installed with its install command. A step skipped for lack of a skill is reported as skipped,
  not as passed.
- **Carry outputs forward verbatim.** Each step's output is the next step's input, as listed in
  `references/workflows.md`. Summarizing between steps loses the evidence the next skill checks.
- **Respect each skill's own gates.** A release gate that says HOLD, a keyword map that is not
  signed off, or a draft the user has not confirmed stops the workflow there. Say so; do not
  route around it.

## Workflow

1. **Classify the goal.** Read the request against the workflow table below. If it fits one
   skill, route there and stop. If it fits more than one workflow, pick the one whose first step the user
   can start now and say which you set aside.
2. **Check what is installed.** Run:

       python scripts/route_check.py espresso      # one brew, by name, number or old W id
       python scripts/route_check.py --all         # every brew

   It reads `references/workflows.md` and looks for each skill's `SKILL.md` under the usual skill
   folders (`~/.claude/skills`, `~/.qoder/skills`, `~/.cursor/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`,
   `.claude/skills` and plugin caches). Add `--path <dir>` for any other location.
3. **Lay out the route.** Open `references/workflows.md` for the chosen workflow and write one
   line per step: skill, what it receives, what it hands on, and whether it is installed. Mark the
   chain skill if one already packages the steps (Brew 1 · Pour-over has `skill-launch`, Brew 3 · Espresso has the
   `release-gate-*` forks, Brew 4 · Cold brew has `seo-polish`, `keyword-resolver` and `seo-sweep`,
   Brew 10 · Descale has `tune-and-ship` for one published skill at a time).
4. **Hand off step 1.** Load the first skill with its input. When a step finishes, come back to
   the route, record the step's verdict or output location, and hand off the next one.
5. **Close the loop.** When the last step finishes, list each step as done, skipped (with the
   reason) or stopped at a gate, plus the one next action.

## The brews

| # | Goal | Steps, in order |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Brew 1 · Pour-over | Build a skill and make it installable | draft-skill or prompts-to-skill → tune-skill → prompts-to-skill-release → skill-to-mod (only if it must run at a fixed moment) |
| Brew 2 · Bloom | Get a repo, skill or plugin found | findable → publish-pipeline → upstream-check → get-indexed (if new pages went live) |
| Brew 3 · Espresso | Decide whether a site is safe to launch | web-preflight → pre-ship-security-red-team → pre-ship-performance-audit → release-gate-chair (or its -ledger and -validator forks) |
| Brew 4 · Cold brew | Grow organic search traffic | seo-crawl → keyword-guard → wordsmith → pre-ship-performance-audit, platform-content, get-indexed (each if it applies) |
| Brew 5 · French press | Land a job | recruiter-lens → applicant-kit → application-pilot → career-track (for an offer, promotion or pivot) |
| Brew 6 · Cupping | Make a decision | research-brief → data-readout (if there is data) → crash-test or do-better → strategy-memo |
| Brew 7 · Slow drip | Learn a skill | topic-primer → study-system → course-builder (only when teaching a group) |
| Brew 8 · Nitro | Run cold outbound | cold-email-list-gate → cold-email-ops → sales-copy |
| Brew 9 · Moka pot | Launch a one-person product | solo-income-blueprint → site-prompt → production-code → paper-trail → Brew 3 · Espresso → platform-content |
| Brew 10 · Descale | Maintain the skill family | tune-skill (regress.py) → prompts-to-skill-release (if behaviour changed) → upstream-check |
| Brew 11 · Estate roast | Stand up or audit a skill estate | skill-estate (eight gated phases over the whole collection) |
| Brew 12 · Dial-in | Set up a coding agent for a repo | portable-harness or harness-audit → setup-claude-advisor (if quota is the constraint) → diagnose-usage (if usage already drained) → choose-effort (before a large task) |

Per-step inputs, outputs and stop conditions are in `references/workflows.md`. Open it at step 3,
and whenever a user asks what one skill needs from the previous one.
`references/trigger-cases.md` holds the hand-run trigger cases; open it when tuning this
description or adding a workflow.

## Report

Lead with the route: workflow number, then one line per step with its status. Then the missing
skills with install commands, any gate that stopped the run, and the one next action. Say which
steps you only planned and which actually ran.

**Route: Brew 3 · Espresso, then Brew 4 · Cold brew.** Your goal needs both. I set aside Brew 9 · Moka pot, because that is for building a product from scratch and yours is already built. I only planned this route. None of the steps have run.

## Brew 3 · Espresso (safe and fast, before launch)

1. **web-preflight** takes your live or staging URL, for a site you own. It hands on one verdict per host: PASS, PASS WITH FIXES, BLOCK or INCONCLUSIVE.
2. **pre-ship-security-red-team** takes your source and an isolated environment, never production. It hands on findings with evidence and a list of what it couldn't test.
3. **pre-ship-performance-audit** takes your source and a build. It hands on measured before and after numbers.
4. **release-gate-chair** takes the three lane reports. It hands on one posture, HOLD or ready, computed by script. **If it says HOLD, the workflow stops and you don't launch.** (`release-gate-ledger` is an alternative.)

## Brew 4 · Cold brew (found on Google, after the gate is ready and the site is live)

1. **seo-crawl** takes your live URL. It hands on findings JSON with stable IDs. It stops if a check is inconclusive and you need that area judged.
2. **keyword-guard** takes the titles, H1s, canonicals and sitemap inventory from step 1. It hands on a keyword map with one owner page per query. **You must sign off the map before the next step.**
3. **wordsmith** takes the approved findings and the map. It hands on rewritten titles, meta descriptions and copy, keeping your facts.
4. **pre-ship-performance-audit** is optional here. Use it only if Core Web Vitals came up.
5. **platform-content** is optional. It takes the owner pages and the map and hands on posts that link back to those pages.
6. **get-indexed** takes the live site once the fixes are deployed and a re-crawl is clean. It sends the changed pages to IndexNow, resubmits the sitemap, and gives you a short list to submit by hand.

Re-run seo-crawl once after the fixes and compare finding IDs. A code change alone doesn't prove a fix.

## Missing skills

None of these are installed, and I won't improvise their work:

```
npx skills add arm-pz/web-preflight
npx skills add arm-pz/pre-ship-security-red-team
npx skills add arm-pz/pre-ship-performance-audit
npx skills add arm-pz/release-gate-chair
npx skills add arm-pz/seo-crawl
npx skills add arm-pz/keyword-guard
npx skills add arm-pz/wordsmith
```

The optional steps, `platform-content` and `get-indexed`, would need installing too if you use them.

## Shortcuts
- `seo-sweep` runs Brew 4 steps 1, 2, 3 and 6, and fixes the findings in your code. `seo-polish` and `keyword-resolver` package smaller parts of it.
- `ship-sentinel` or the `release-gate-mod` plugin can block `git push` and deploys until the gate has run.

## Next action
Install the four Brew 3 skills, then start step 1 with `web-preflight` on your staging URL. Run Brew 4 once the gate is ready and the site is live. Do you want me to start step 1 once they're installed?
